diagrams.title: SOAR Workflow: From Alert to Bounded Action
diagrams.subtitle: A playbook coordinates SIEM, enrichment, decision, action, and verification. Guardrails bound every output.

nodes.label: Trigger
nodes.detail: An alert or external signal launches the playbook. The trigger must be precise to avoid unnecessary executions.
nodes.exam: A playbook without a qualified trigger amplifies false positives.

nodes.label: Enrichment
nodes.detail: Queries reputation databases, connection history, and the criticality of targeted assets.
nodes.exam: Enrichment precedes decision: it reduces noise.

nodes.label: Decision
nodes.detail: Documented logic evaluates the risk score; above a threshold, human approval may be required.
nodes.exam: Automation logic must be understood and tested before deployment.

nodes.label: Guardrails
nodes.detail: Limits imposed on the action: reduced scope, bounded duration, logging, approval, and rollback capability.
nodes.exam: Without guardrails, a triage mistake is applied at machine speed.

nodes.label: Action
nodes.detail: IP block on the firewall, configuration change, ticket creation: the action is reversible and logged.
nodes.exam: Orchestration chains multiple tools; automation executes a task.

nodes.label: Verification
nodes.detail: Checks the effect, monitors false positives, then tunes the playbook — continuous improvement.

nodes.label: Agentic AI
nodes.detail: Agentic AI can plan and execute a sequence of actions; it requires explicit guardrails. Outside the books, §4.6.
nodes.exam: Agentic AI ≠ chatbot: the agent acts, it doesn't just reply.

quiz.question: Which node limits the scope, duration, and reversibility of an automated action?
